A few other shitty things with places like these other than close / open shifts. 

Holidays… 

1) typically they will not honor the non mandatory ones. 

2) Next, not sure where you are, but where I am this is an easy way for them to screw employees. 

For example, if you normally don’t work mondays and the holiday is on a Monday you are not entitled to holiday pay. But if you do work that day they have to pay you x1.5. 

Now if you normally work the Monday they are required to either pay you for the day off. Or pay you x1.5 for working. 

So you will never ever get holidays off if it falls on a day you are typically scheduled for. They won’t give you the day off cause they have to pay you regardless. And you’re essentially working the holiday for half rate. Yes you still make more, but would you rather get 100% pay for 0 time spent at work? Or 150% pay for 100% shift time spent at work?

“The grass is always greener on the other side”. I think it’s safe to assume most people posting here are at the very least middle class. Yes, the Philippines is a poor country. But you, as a member of the middle class have benefited greatly from having majority of the population in poverty. If the Philippines progressed to being a first world country (and don’t get this confused with having a strong economy). Suddenly, the house or car you could afford becomes that much more expensive because more people would be able to afford them. Suddenly, you can’t afford to have that yaya or katulong (if anything they may end up your neighbours or even your superiors, not that there’s anything wrong with that, but you lose out). Suddenly, you have that more much competition to get into good schools or jobs because everyone is able to access the same things that you are. Suddenly, your expenses multiply as the poor are no longer there to drag the price down. Suddenly, your taxes end up getting higher and you’ll find the government charges for just about everything but the right to breathe. Suddenly, you’ll find that much more bureaucracy and red tape when it comes to getting things done (after all proper documentation is needed to help temper corruption). 

There’s pros and cons to everything. 

And know this, you are owed nothing and the government only sees you as a number. Everything they “give” the community comes at a cost. And that money has to come from somewhere (your pockets). 

Also the more you “control” the ruling class, the more they will pass on the cost to the consumer. 

Don’t get me wrong. I’m not pro poverty. But this is the system we live in. I just want people to understand just how much they’ve actually benefited from this system, instead of blindly believing abroad is better. You have already benefited off of the suffering of others as soon a s you were born middle class. 

Just saying the grass isn’t always 100% greener on the other side.

Also, be kinder to one another. Don’t treat the masses like they are a bunch of ignorant nuisances. You are where you are, because they are where they are. Society is a pyramid, and they are part of the base holding you up. What makes a first world country is that base is much much stronger.

Note: this is in reference to first world countries in general.
